title: After the rollout an AccountingHub organization has all starting mappings
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use the production test account.
  • Use an organization on AccountingHub before the release, and note its chart of accounts and Account Mappings before the release.
custom_steps:
1. Open Accounting > Account Mappings.
  2. Open Accounting's chart of accounts.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • All four starting category rows are mapped, Comeback included: General Internal to a Vehicle Expenses account, Warranty and Goodwill to a Warranty & Goodwill Expense account, Comeback to a Comeback Expense account.
  • Every mapping noted before the release that was valid still points at the same account.

Step 2:

  • An active expense account whose name matched was reused, not duplicated.
  • A missing account was created; if its default number was taken by an unrelated account, it sits at a free number and that account keeps its name and number.
  • An existing account was reused when its name matched ignoring letter case, spaces and "&" against "and".
  • A renamed 6500 was not reused: a new "Vehicle Expenses" sits at a free number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11763 (Story 6, AccountingHub account mapping), story SV-12295 (Story 13, Release day, seeding and migration)

  • S6-R2: “Automatically set up the starting category mappings using AccountingHub's existing chart of accounts. General Internal defaults to 6500 Vehicle Expenses, already in the default chart. Warranty and Goodwill both default to 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense, already in the newer chart. Comeback defaults to 6440 Comeback Expense, a new required account (number confirmed by the AccountingHub owner on 2026-11-09). The existing 6400 Shop Equipment Maintenance account remains available for accountants to select where appropriate; it is not an additional starting category. The mapping key should allow a kind (parts, labor) later, so V2 adds rows instead of changing the contract.”
  • S13-R3: “The AccountingHub setup of S6-R2 runs as an operator command, not a deploy migration: organization by organization in isolation, with a list of failures and a verify mode; it runs after the hub release and again at launch. For each organization it reuses suitable accounts (an active expense account whose name matches), creates missing ones (6430 on a legacy chart too, 6440 Comeback Expense), populates every starting-category mapping, preserves valid mappings and resolves number conflicts with a free number. New organizations get the same set from the seeder.”
  • S13-E1: “A hub organization whose chart already uses the Comeback default number for an unrelated account gets Comeback Expense at a free number (S6-R2); the mapping is populated all the same.”
  • S13-R5: “Verification after the run, per organization: four categories, four QuickBooks rows per connected location, four hub mappings populated (Comeback included), the setting off. The rule-zero verify of S9-R14 runs the same day. If engineering ships the feature behind a deploy switch until launch day, the switch is removed with the launch and is not a product setting (Key Decisions, No feature flag).”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026
